questions.question: What is the difference between revising, editing and proofreading?
options: Revising improves content and organization; editing fixes sentence-level issues; proofreading catches surface errors
They are three words for the same activity
Editing means deleting the whole text
questions.explanation: Revising = big picture, editing = sentence level (grammar, clarity), proofreading = final check for typos and spelling.

questions.question: What does the ARMS revision strategy stand for?
questions.explanation: ARMS: Add what is missing, Remove the unnecessary, Move what is misplaced, Substitute what could be better.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the writing process?
questions.explanation: The process moves from planning (prewriting) through drafting and revising to editing and final proofreading.

questions.question: Which is an effective revision tip?
options: Take time away from your text before revising, and read it aloud
Revise immediately while the text is fresh in your mind
Never let anyone else read your draft
questions.explanation: Distance helps you see your text objectively; reading aloud reveals awkward sentences and errors.

questions.question: What is a reverse outline used for?
options: Checking the structure of a draft you have already written
Counting the words in each paragraph
questions.explanation: A reverse outline summarises each paragraph of your draft so you can evaluate and fix the overall structure.
